anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: The workload issues overly broad, chatty, or long-running statements/transactions that fetch, scan, or lock more data than business logic requires.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly: The database engine grows buffer pools, work areas, and other heaps beyond the safe capacity of the host, inducing paging, swapping, or OOM conditions.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly: Physical data, temp, or log volumes reach or exceed their sustained IOPS/throughput limits, driving up device-level latency and queue depths.

When all three root causes coexist, end-to-end latency escalates sharply: chatty or scan-heavy SQL floods the buffer cache and temp space, inflating per-query work memory and provoking aggressive cache growth. Memory pressure triggers paging, which redirects random and spill-to-disk access to already saturated storage; in turn, the overtaxed I/O subsystem elongates read, write, and checkpoint times, further stretching transaction duration and increasing the number of concurrent sessions and memory consumers. Observables include skyrocketing resident-set size, frequent page-in/page-out activity, plan-cache and work-memory bloat, sustained disk queues, elevated buffer-I/O and log flush waits, and application timeouts with retries that multiply the load.

Causally, inefficient SQL amplifies both memory and I/O demand by expanding result sets, causing large sorts/hashes, and keeping transactions open longer. The expansion forces the engine to allocate more buffers and work areas, pushing the host toward memory exhaustion. As the OS begins to swap, every logical read can devolve into a physical I/O, compounding the storage bottleneck. Simultaneously, the storage subsystem’s throttling feeds back into the database, slowing buffer flushes and extending transaction lifetimes, which keeps memory allocations active and magnifies plan-cache and session-state footprints. The reinforcing loop among bloated workload logic, unchecked memory growth, and saturated storage throughput degrades both throughput and stability, ultimately risking node eviction or service outage.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle, but not within an open transaction, for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle and not inside an open transaction longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; the documentation warns about using this with connection pools or middleware.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
